title: Frenkie de Jong & Marc-Andre Stegen included in Barcelona squad for pre-season trip to England
summary: Barcelona named a 30-man squad for a pre-season training camp in England, with friendlies against Birmingham City and Preston. Marc-Andre ter Stegen is included despite ongoing loan talks with Ajax, while Frenkie de Jong is in the travelling party but will not play because of a knee injury. Hansi Flick will use the trip at St George's Park to assess young players and new signing Karim Adeyemi, with Fermin López and Ronald Araujo continuing their recoveries.
content:
A few surprises appeared in Barcelona's travelling party for their pre-season training camp in England.

Barcelona have named a 30-man travelling squad for their pre-season training camp in England that will feature friendlies against Birmingham City and Preston. The players are due to fly out shortly and will head to England’s training base at St George’s Park which will be their home for the next week.

Marc-Andre ter Stegen is on the list despite being in talks to leave on loan for Ajax, while Frenkie de Jong is also in the squad but won’t play due to a knee injury.

Here’s a look at the full squad list.

Goalkeepers: Marc-Andre ter Stegen, Aron Yaakobishvili, Wojciech Szczęsny, Iker Rodríguez.

Defenders: Hector Fort, Alejandro Balde, Ronald Araujo, Alvaro Cortés, Xavi Espart, Andreas Christensen, Gerard Martin, Jofre Torrents, Jordi Pesquer.

Midfielders: Guille Fernández, Brian Fariñas, Tommy Marques, Fermín López, Marc Casadó, Marc Bernal, Ibrahim Diarra, Frenkie de Jong, Orian Goren.

Forwards: Hamza Abdelkarim, Toni Fernández, Alex González, Ebrima Tunkara, Karim Adeyemi, Roony Bardghji, Shane Kluivert, Òscar Gistau.

The camp will give Hansi Flick the chance to continue to check on a raft of impressive young stars as well as new signing Karim Adeyemi. Several youngsters have been included so the manager can assess their readiness ahead of the season.

Fermín López and Ronald Araujo are also part of the squad as they work their way back from injuries. The club will manage minutes carefully in the friendlies and training sessions to protect players returning from knocks.

Barcelona have already staged a behind-closed-doors match as part of their preparations and will use the week at St George’s Park to build fitness, sharpen tactics and finalise plans ahead of the new campaign.
